name: easyeda-pro-control
description: Safety-gated EasyEDA adapters, narrow symbol/PCB workflows and seven engineering skills.

interface.longDescription: Seven skills cover control, schematics, PCB layout, libraries, manufacturing, design review and extensions. The API inventory distinguishes public subsets, native equivalents, blocked implementations and omissions. A separate no-editor project PCB reader returns bounded native metadata without opening a canvas, requesting Save or granting rename authority. Read-only PCB rename preflight additionally compares expected metadata and complete native PCB peers, observes actual native title availability, and collects client/ticket and UI actor/clock samples. These observations do not establish native producer ownership, backend clocks, saved state or writer authority; installed121700 passed one disposable read-only preflight with unchanged complete raw/SQL/native data after normal closure. A separate disposable PCB title-change tool now retains original PCB ownership, startup/actor/dual-clock checks, one fixed native update, full closed SQL effect and fresh saved metadata verification. Its writer still needs connected validation. Ordinary-project PCB rename, linked reuse propagation, drawing changes and inverse remain unsupported. The current reviewed tuple provides calculations, environment/unit and editor metadata, PCB layer/identity/geometry reads, Component metadata, Pad parameters, component child-pad lists and parentless String text. String readers preserve raw text/font, pose/style in mil/degrees, key/show flags, positionIsNull and serialized silkColor. Native-normalized color is not raw-model color proof; component attributes, rendered glyphs and saved-source ownership remain excluded. Polygon paths, complete stacks, resolved rules, reverse ownership and schematic pin mapping remain unverified. A project-local symbol metadata reader observes exact name, description, tags, template reference, version and ticket without geometry loading or cloud-library fallback. That PCB-context read proves neither hidden-editor absence nor a safe rename baseline. A separate project-only preflight compares caller-supplied expected metadata while excluding editor tabs and hidden frames. It also observes bounded UI actor, client, ticket and clock samples. Caller expectations are not provenance; backend actor/clock, permission, startup completion, saved membership and writer authority remain unverified. Ordinary existing-profile launch, retained-owner window observation and one-shot normal closure support disposable project/PCB opening. Baseline validation retains closed SQL evidence, relaunches and opens only the project with fresh source/cache checks and a startup-prefix observation. Its finish actions normally close the retained replacement generation. After proved termination they preserve a final closed raw SQL/native snapshot before releasing captures. Snapshot failure remains distinct from retirement and never permits replay. Offline baseline analysis compares both retained snapshots without reading the original project. Retirement clock reports describe sampled native clocks, not backend actor or timestamp-producer qualification. These baseline actions neither execute the prepared symbol patch nor prove startup completion or writer readiness. Separate disposable validation actions require an unreferenced symbol with complete META-only history or a bounded canvas-segments profile. That canvas profile allows at most 101 complete history chunks including reserved writes, preserves exact drawing lines and admits only orders attainable by the pinned concurrent replay. Stable atom types, lossless bodies, unambiguous cache actors, a unique latest/max-ticket header and strictly later document windows with inverse headroom are required. Installed210000 passed this disposable canvas-segments forward/inverse round trip with complete closed SQL, reopened content, metadata restoration and final closure. Pre-write checks reserve bounded history, SQL and saved-result capacity; physical file growth and resource completion remain runtime limitations. Native linked-sheet propagation is unsupported. They can dispatch one sealed symbol name/description edit and its internally derived inverse, each requiring exact-phase acknowledgements and complete closed SQL plus reopened-content verification. Installed101500 passed a complete disposable forward/inverse round trip with closed SQL, reopened-content and metadata-restoration verification. The separate easyeda_control_project_symbol_metadata route now exposes forward-only name and/or non-null description changes for unused symbols with complete META-only or supported bounded canvas-segments history and original-owner checks. Ordinary edits reserve exactly one write and expose no inverse. Installed123000 passed that ordinary unused META-only forward-only entrypoint with exact closed SQL, reopened saved content, final SQL equality and retained process closure. Historical evidence grants no current-invocation authority. Installed080000 passed the ordinary unused drawn-symbol forward lifecycle with complete closed SQL, exact reopened content and final closure on a disposable fixture. A separate disposable-only symbol-copy tool consumes the original disposable opening and complete closed SQL baseline. It copies one supported single-part self-contained drawing through a fixed native clone, retaining the returned UUID and exact derived title. It requires startup, actor, dual-clock and capacity checks before one attempt, complete closed SQL effect verification and cache-excluded saved reopening afterward. Source and peer SQL must remain unchanged. Ordinary copying, caller-chosen names/classifications, external assets, explicit Save and deletion/inverse remain unsupported. Installed094000 passed one disposable supported drawn-symbol copy with complete closed SQL, exact reopened content, unchanged source/peers and final closure. Later generations and other source histories remain unvalidated. Generic design and library writers remain disabled. A failed disposable opener can request one normal close through its original retained Job without bridge dispatch, keeping quarantine until terminal retirement. Ordinary opening waits for a bounded native startup-prefix event, not full restoration completion. Closure never chooses Save/Discard or forces exit; acknowledgment and retained termination are separate. Opening can migrate storage and automatically Save. Lost handles, ambiguous launch and quarantine retain their restrictions; inspection never replays operations. Historical abandonment qualifies only specific evidence. The older tuple retains separately guarded readers, footprint typed API operations, native controls, checkpoints and recovery. Legacy schematic-page, symbol and PCB transaction routes plus their eight metadata writers remain blocked pending current lifecycle adaptation, native structure-job completion and complete SQL-effect proof. Compiled topology and affected exports refuse hidden annotation or Save All. Connected validation is operation- and generation-specific. Arbitrary JavaScript, blind retries and unrestricted Save remain refused. The legacy writer is runtime-disabled. Missing installation files select offline-only startup. The historical reviewed tuple is connected-read-admitted; future mismatches fail closed within each capability profile.
defaultPrompt: Validate the EasyEDA bridge without bypassing compatibility gates.
Inspect the admitted EasyEDA project with exact readers and managed evidence.
Apply the requested typed design change and verify it after saving and reopening.
